head.h1: Breakfast Catering in Dubai — Real Prices, Menus and Timings

opening_paragraph: Breakfast catering in Dubai from myCHEF starts at AED 90 per person for a drop-off and AED 120 per person for a staffed buffet. A fresh morning spread — pastries, fruit, hot stations and proper coffee — is served at your home or office. A vetted private chef plans the menu, cooks it fresh, serves and clears away, so the morning stays yours. Give us the date, guest count and venue; we typically reply within 15 minutes during business hours, with a full itemised quote to follow, and we build every spread around your taste, your guests and any dietary needs.

new_paragraphs: We deliver breakfast catering across Dubai, so "breakfast catering near me" reaches homes, villas and offices citywide — Downtown, Business Bay, DIFC, Dubai Marina, JBR, Palm Jumeirah, Jumeirah, Emirates Hills, Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills and the wider communities. Office kitchens, rooftop terraces, garden villas and serviced apartments are all part of a normal week, and we plan access, timing and set-up to each address. add_block.new_heading: The breakfast catering Dubai menu — course by course, brunch and high tea included
new_paragraphs: Below is the full working menu, in the order a Dubai morning is served: the pastry basket and cold table first, hot Arabic and continental dishes behind them, live stations to one side, and the three-tier stand if the booking runs into the afternoon. Nothing here is a category placeholder. Pick a spread from it, or send it back with your own edits and the chefs build from there. Volume formats start at 10 guests, and 20 for a buffet line.
Bakery and viennoiserie — the pastry basket
Every continental spread opens here, and it is the first thing your guests form an opinion about.
Viennoiserie: all-butter croissants · pain au chocolat · almond croissants · custard Danish · pineapple Danish · assorted fruit Danish pastries.
Miniatures: mini flavoured croissants in caramel and pistachio · mini muffins, feta and olive or raspberry almond · cinnamon snails.

Breads: a bread station of white, whole wheat and sourdough · artisanal sourdough with preserves · bagels and toast with spreads · artisanal baguettes · banana bread · orange blossom scones · sausage rolls.
The cold table — dairy, cheese and preserves
Levantine and continental mornings share this table, laid out on brass trays with warm pita coming from the kitchen in rounds.
Labneh and cheese: labneh · walnut labneh · zaatar labneh · garlic labneh · shanklish · grilled halloumi · akkawi cheese · Nabulsi cheese boats.
Cured and cold cuts: French cheeses and cold cuts · smoked salmon · chicken mortadella and cheese in ciabatta.
Preserves: makdous · olives and fresh vegetables with warm pita · house-made jams · rose jam · date syrup (dibs) and local honey.
Yoghurt, parfaits and wellness bowls
This section is what separates a 2026 breakfast menu from a 2015 one, and it is the part corporate bookers ask about first.
Grains and oats: bircher muesli · toasted muesli · overnight oats · berry porridge · whole grain cereals.

Jars and pots, portioned per guest: Greek yoghurt with honey · yoghurt granola pots · chia pudding · berry chia pudding · five berry breakfast jam jar · bircher muesli jam jar · banana and honey jam jar · apple crumble jam jar · polenta pears jam jar.
Bowls: black chia bowl on a coconut milk base · açaí bowl with granola, peanut butter and fruit · pitaya smoothie pots · green morning bowl of spinach, avocado and seeds.
Fruit and juice
Fruit: seasonal fruit platter · fresh fruit salad · seasonal fruit skewers · fruit canapé box · fruit in cup box · individual exotic fruit salad with honey cinnamon yoghurt.
Juice: freshly squeezed orange · watermelon · cold-pressed detox juices · classic lemonade · berry fruit drink · an infused water station.
Hot breakfast — continental
Halal by default, so the Western plate is rebuilt with turkey bacon, beef bacon, chicken sausage and turkey ham.
Eggs: scrambled eggs with toppings · poached eggs · cheese omelette · eggs Benedict on brioche · individual quiche Alsacienne · mini quiches, vegetarian and chicken · frittatas.
From the griddle: French toast · mini pancakes · Belgian waffles · corn fritters · sweet potato rosti with poached eggs · croque-monsieur with gruyere, smoked sausage and pickled red onion.
Sides: hash browns · sautéed mushrooms · grilled tomatoes · baked beans · grilled chicken sausages · grilled turkey bacon.
Hot breakfast — Arabic and Levantine
This is the section Dubai buyers judge a caterer on, so it is written out dish by dish instead of hidden behind the words "Arabic selection".
Beans and eggs: foul medammas · balila, warm fava beans and chickpeas · shakshouka · eggs and sujouk · eggs and makanek · eggs and potato · eggs your way.
Fatteh and fried: hummus fatteh · eggplant fatteh · falafel.
From the saj and the oven: manakish zaatar · manakish cheese · lahm bi ajine · spinach fatayer · mini fatayer · knefeh.
Emirati Fuala — the local-heritage table
Fuala is served morning and evening, and it is the table Emirati hosts look for at a family gathering or a Ramadan morning.
Savoury: balaleet, saffron vermicelli with omelette · chebab, Emirati pancakes with date syrup · khameer bread · khubz regag · regag with cheese · dango · bajella.
Sweet and gahwa: aseed · khabeesah, a pumpkin mash · al batheetha · luqaimat with date syrup · dates with date molasses · gahwa poured with cardamom.
Indian and South Asian breakfast
Aloo paratha with chana masala · channa masala with paratha · masala dosa with sambar · idli · ragi idli · medu vada · upma · poha · fruit chaat · masala chai and karak.
Rolls, bagels and wraps — the drop-off and grab-and-go backbone
Pre-wrapped, single-hand food for a counter by the entrance, or boxed and labelled per guest for a desk drop.

Rolls and bagels: smoked salmon, pickled cucumber, red onion and mayonnaise bagel · free-range egg, turkey bacon, mayo and roasted tomato roll · sausage, turkey bacon, egg and tomato relish · portobello mushroom, egg, spinach and caramelised onion.
Croissants: tomato and emmental · Swiss cheese croissant with egg, turkey ham and tomato · croissant with salmon.
Sourdough and rye: halloumi and avocado on sourdough · smashed avocado on rye with smoked bresaola, quail egg and a fennel dill salad.
Wraps: halloumi wrap · egg and cheese wrap · spinach, mushroom and grilled halloumi pesto wrap · vegetarian frittata wrap with roasted peppers and feta · breakfast burritos · breakfast tacos.
Sandwiches: cheese and tomato in brown bread · boiled egg, mayonnaise and mustard cress in multi-cereal bread.
Brunch canapés and bowl-and-fork
The upmarket tier, built for a standing brunch where nobody sits down.

Cold: asparagus, poached quail egg, Taleggio and baguette en croûte (V) · smoked salmon with a sour cream and chive blini, pickled gherkin and mustard cress · cured mackerel, pickled fennel and horseradish crème fraîche on a poppy-seed bagel · wagyu beef cannoli with beetroot, spiced ricotta, baby herbs and sumac thyme sea salt · crab, salmon and caviar on a crumpet.

Hot: rolled omelette with wilted spinach, sausage and roasted tomato · shawarma breakfast pies with roasted tomato, spinach and egg · pepper steak and mushroom pie · chicken, asparagus and Taleggio pie · pumpkin and sage calzone with semi-dried tomatoes, buffalo mozzarella and basil · smoked chicken apple sausage egg slider · mini scotch eggs.

Bowl-and-fork: Sri Lankan egg hoppers with green sambal, split peas, sauté kale and coconut gel (V) · big breakfast waffle with wilted spinach, sausage and roasted tomato · chicken waffle with pickled fennel, roquette and a lemon dill seeded mustard dressing · ocean trout crêpes in brioche · pumpkin, spinach, mascarpone and oven-roasted tomatoes on scones (V).
Brunch salads and the grazing table

Composed salads: grilled Mediterranean vegetables with Persian feta, pesto and a baby herb salad (V) · cauliflower, quinoa, roasted fig, pomegranate, labneh, mint and orange blossom dressing (V) · roasted beetroot with peaches, white asparagus, savoury granola, cinnamon basil and verjuice (V) · heirloom tomato with Asiago, olive soil and house vinaigrette (V).

Grains and classics: Middle Eastern scented pilaf with raisins, coconut, coriander, honey and cumin vinaigrette · pickled carrot, pearl barley, dates, raisins, pine nuts, candied hibiscus and a zaatar lemon vinaigrette (V) · Caesar with garlic en croûte, quail eggs, turkey bacon and white anchovies · tuna niçoise with heirloom tomatoes, olives, chat potatoes and white anchovies.

Grazing boards: a cheddar and blue cheese platter · antipasti and cheese box · fresh vegetable platter · bruschetta caprese · sun-dried tomato bruschetta · salmon bruschetta · mini Greek salads with feta · mini salads with salmon.
Live stations, cooked in front of your guests
Stations sit on top of a buffet, not instead of one, and the theatre is half of what you are booking. Two to four is a normal count for a morning event.

Eggs and griddle: an omelette station made to order — plain, cheese, mushroom, turkey ham, beef bacon · shakshuka in individual cast-iron pans · a Belgian waffle station · a pancake station with a toppings bar.
Crepes, sweet and savoury: Nutella, strawberry and banana on one side; olives, grilled vegetables and assorted cheeses on the other.
Regional counters: a live saj turning out manakish · a dosa and idli counter · a luqaimat and regag station · jalebi with rabri.
Drinks and wellness: a barista coffee and juice bar · a wellness grain and açaí bar · a live bread-making station.
High tea — the savoury tier
Bottom tier of the three-tier stand, cut into fingers and halved so the tray reads properly.
Finger sandwiches: egg mayonnaise · cucumber · coronation-style chicken · Norwegian salmon with horseradish · smoked salmon and cream cheese · roast smoked beef with caramelised onion.
Pastry savouries: mini quiches · mini rolls · salmon and cream cheese tartlets · mushroom and cucumber canapés.
High tea — the scone tier
Scones: plain · fruit and raisin · chocolate · orange blossom.
To go with them: clotted cream · house preserves · lemon curd.
High tea — the sweet tier and petit fours
Patisserie: assorted macarons · pistachio macaroons · éclairs · profiteroles · matcha choux buns with a craquelin topping and vanilla yuzu custard · orange blossom madeleines · marmalade financier.
Tarts and cakes: lemon and lime tarts · lemon meringue tart · mini cheesecakes · chocolate brownies · chocolate, macadamia and pear brownie · cupcakes · Battenberg cake · panforte.
Petit fours: assorted chocolate truffles · almond and pistachio biscotti · cherry, rose water and hazelnut nougat · oatmeal cookies with walnuts.
The Traditional Set — Arabic and Emirati high tea
Booked as often as the international stand, and the two run side by side at a ladies' gathering or a Fuala in the evening.
Luqaimat · regag with cheese · Um Ali · Omani halwa · dates · saffron pastries · karak tea · red tea · Arabic coffee.
Coffee, tea and cold drinks
Coffee: flat white, cortado, long black and cappuccino from a speciality roast · cold brew · Lebanese coffee · Arabic coffee with cardamom · matcha · beetroot latte.
Tea: Earl Grey · Darjeeling · Moroccan mint · oud · saffron-rose · herbal infusions · karak chai.
Cold: freshly squeezed juices · smoothies · still and sparkling water.
Sweet finish, for a brunch that runs past midday

Japanese fluffy air pancake · chocolate thyme pancakes with maple syrup ice cream and honey handkerchiefs · chocolate truffle waffle with vanilla Chantilly and stone fruit compote · apple, rosemary salted caramel, candied orange and brioche · strudel · dessert profiteroles · strawberry and marshmallow platter · crème brûlée jam jar · brownie jam jar.
How the menu is served, and what to tell us

The same dishes are laid out differently depending on the morning. A hot chafing line with a cold bakery table is the default above 30 guests. A continental credenza with no hot line suits a boardroom start. Individual boxes, labelled per guest, are the fastest-moving office format in Dubai right now, and a grab-and-go bar by the entrance works when people are walking through instead of sitting down. Drop-off platters are sized by the number of people they serve. High tea comes on three-tier stands, or packed as a takeaway stand.

Dietary flags are marked inline against each dish — (V) for vegetarian — instead of buried in a note at the bottom. Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event.

On timing, treat these as guidance. A standard breakfast catering package sits at about 72 hours' notice, live stations and multi-staff mornings at 3 to 5 days, a bespoke menu at 5 to 7 days, and a wedding-morning or large corporate production at 7 to 14 days or more. We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. A breakfast at short notice is sometimes workable - availability is confirmed individually, never assumed.

add_block.new_heading: How much does breakfast catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Breakfast catering in Dubai starts at AED 90 per person for a drop-off or boxed office breakfast, AED 120 per person for a staffed buffet and AED 150 per person once live egg, pancake or pastry stations are on the floor. A private chef who cooks and plates breakfast in front of a small table is a different product at AED 700 to AED 950 per person. What separates the tiers is staff and cooking on site, not the quality of the pastry. The itemised quote shows food, staff, equipment and delivery on separate lines, so you can take one out and watch the total move. Volume formats need 10 guests, a buffet needs 20, the minimum order is AED 900, and 5% VAT is added to every total. For the same breakdown across other cuisines and formats, see our Dubai catering price guide . It is the honest answer to what the best breakfast catering in Dubai should cost.
How much is breakfast in Dubai, and what does cheap breakfast catering buy?

For one person eating out, a Dubai breakfast runs from a few dirhams at a neighbourhood bakery to well over a hundred at a hotel counter, so catering has to be judged per head on the same scale. Our entry tier is AED 90 per person, and for 10 guests that is the AED 900 minimum order. It buys a genuine spread delivered ready to serve: viennoiserie, a cold table with labneh and cheese, fruit, juice and coffee, with no staff on site. That is what cheap breakfast catering honestly looks like in Dubai, and it is the tier most office mornings should book. AED 120 adds people who set it out, keep the hot line hot and clear it away afterwards. AED 150 puts a chef behind an egg or pancake station. Anything advertised far below the entry tier is usually a pastry box count instead of a breakfast, so ask what the per-head figure includes before you compare it with ours.
Breakfast platters, finger food and the lunch that follows

Two formats sit either side of a served breakfast. Breakfast platters in Dubai are the drop-off version: viennoiserie, a fruit platter, a labneh and cheese board and a juice run, sized by the number of people they feed and delivered ready to put on a table. Finger food catering is the standing version of the same idea, built for a room where people are holding a coffee and talking rather than sitting down — mini croissants, filled brioche, zaatar and cheese manakish cut into fingers, skewered fruit, and bite-sized pastries that survive an hour on a table. Both start at the AED 90 drop-off tier. If the morning runs into a working session, the sensible move is to book breakfast and lunch catering on one order, so the same team handles both deliveries and the clear-down happens once; see business lunch catering for how the midday half is priced.

add_block.new_heading: Why book breakfast catering with myCHEF
new_paragraphs: MyCHEF was founded by a chef trained in some of Europe's most demanding kitchens, on one idea: you own the morning, we carry the work. MyCHEF is implementing a structured 12-stage partner verification and quality-assurance framework across its culinary partner network, covering company identity, trade licence and permitted activities, food-safety permits, Person-in-Charge and food-handler training documentation, allergen controls, and a chef and service-team assessment. We are honest about it, too: no system removes every risk, so each event is matched to the chef well suited to it.

For a breakfast, that is often Ahmed Al-Rashid , whose 18+ years across Dubai, London and Paris in classical French technique show in the way he times a morning — pastries warm, eggs to order, coffee flowing, every element served at its peak. When a spread leans Mediterranean or Italian we bring in Marco Rossi , and for Arabic and halal mornings during Ramadan and beyond, Layla Hassan . Alongside breakfast catering we have delivered villa weddings, yacht celebrations and corporate galas in Dubai. Real client reviews for Breakfast catering are published as events happen.
